decided.claim: Reveal goes through the org.freedesktop.FileManager1.ShowItems session-bus method rather than probing for a specific file manager: it is the one contract Nautilus, Dolphin, Nemo, Caja, Thunar, PCManFM-Qt and elementary Files all export, and D-Bus activation starts whichever one the desktop actually has.

Three legs in order — gdbus, then dbus-send with --print-reply, then a degrade to xdg-open on the containing DIRECTORY (unselected but not silent) — and the whole chain runs on a detached std::thread, because deciding whether to try the next leg means waiting on the previous one, which the UI thread may not do.

The path is percent-encoded into a file:// URI by path_to_file_uri before it reaches any argv; that is both the form ShowItems takes and what leaves no space, quote or backslash in the gdbus GVariant literal, so awkward names need no separate escaping layer.

One pure function, link_local_path, decides revealability over whatever link_under already produced (a resolved absolute path, or a file:// URI); a web URL yields None, and that single None is what keeps reveal off http links at both call sites. A file:// URI with a non-empty, non-localhost authority is refused as a remote share.

The Super+Ctrl branch is tested BEFORE the existing Shift-/Ctrl-click open branch in on_mouse_down, since Ctrl is held for both and the open branch would otherwise swallow the chord; a Super+Ctrl-click on a non-revealable link falls through to the existing open behaviour rather than doing nothing.

The right-click menu's "Reveal in file manager" row is emitted only when revealable_path returns Some, is computed before the link String moves into the Open listener, and carries a hardcoded English label like its Copy/Paste/Open siblings — those labels are not routed through lang.rs.

The chord is made discoverable in the help modal's LINKS section, which the repo's idiom prices at two new Strings keys (k_super_ctrl_click, reveal_link) filled in for all nine languages; a chord in no help modal is a hidden feature.
Recorded as a user-visible feature in [Unreleased]/Added, and the info.html kiosk's Terminal-core bullet list updated to name the reveal chord and the new menu entry.

least_confident.why: The dbus-send leg rests on reasoning I could not execute: without --print-reply dbus-send fires and forgets and exits 0 even with nothing listening, which would swallow the degrade, so I added it — but I never ran either command. I am also unsure a second D-Bus client earns its place at all rather than going straight from gdbus to the degrade.

Super+Ctrl-click on an http link currently OPENS it, because it falls through into the Shift-/Ctrl branch. I read the brief's "it keeps the existing open behaviour" as sanctioning that, but a reader could just as reasonably expect the reveal chord to do nothing at all on a web URL.

Nine translations are mine and unreviewed, and the whole help-modal row is arguably past what a ticket asking for a chord and a menu entry wanted — it is the largest piece of the diff that nobody asked for.

not_done.claim: Nothing was compiled, tested, formatted or linted — no cargo check, test, fmt or clippy.
not_done.why: Builds are out of scope for this exercise, so every claim about compilation, rustfmt shape and test outcomes rests on reading only. The three new tests have never run.

not_done.claim: The reveal itself is unverified end to end.
not_done.why: No compositor or desktop session here, so ShowItems was never exercised against a real file manager, the degrade never fired, and the item-selected behaviour for a directory target was never observed.

not_done.claim: Whether the compositor delivers Super+Ctrl+LeftClick to the window at all is unverified.
not_done.why: Hyprland/Omarchy binds Super+LMB to move-window. Super+Ctrl should not match that exact modmask, but I could not test it, and if it is swallowed the chord is dead on the repo's own primary desktop.

not_done.claim: gpui's mapping of the Super key onto Modifiers::platform on X11/Wayland was not read at the source.
not_done.why: The gpui checkout is a sibling path not present in this tree; I inferred it from in-repo usage (paint_key's `plain` test excludes control/alt/platform).

not_done.claim: A bare absolute path containing a space still cannot be revealed.
not_done.why: link_at tokenises on whitespace and never sees such a path as one link — pre-existing, and widening it is a different change. Only the file:// shape carries a space through, which the tests cover.

not_done.claim: lang.rs's `rclick` summary ("Copy · Paste · Open link · Clear") was not extended to name Reveal.
not_done.why: The entry is conditional on the link being local, the line is already long, and it would have cost nine more translations for a summary rather than an affordance.

not_done.claim: No hover affordance, cursor change, or OSC-8 hyperlink handling for the reveal chord.
not_done.why: Not asked for, and the existing open chord has none either — adding one only for reveal would make the pair inconsistent.

not_done.claim: revealable_path stats the filesystem on every render frame while the context menu is open.
not_done.why: It matches what link_under already does on the same path in the same closure, so it changes no cost profile, but it is unmeasured.
